facts.statement: Does-it-trigger questions are trigger-testing, the wrong track; retrieval testing measures the skill body
A skill whose fact inventory is empty needs no retrieval testing; stop instead of fabricating queries
The harness is always user-specified with no default; prompt for it when missing
Consume exit codes and JSON from harness scripts only; never parse their prose stdout
Both eval workspaces are initialized with --prefix retrieval-test, never the trigger-test prefix
Sync only the skill workspace with the skill; the control workspace is never synced
One contaminated control baseline voids the whole campaign
Skill arm: skill allow, read/grep/glob/list allowed, edit/bash/task/todowrite/webfetch/websearch/question denied; control arm identical except skill deny
Neither eval agent pins model/variant/temperature/top_p; campaign --model/--variant flags are the only model-selection path
The skill under test is force-loaded by instruction in every scenario; the per-run prompt is the bare query
bash is denied, so a skill whose value includes executable scripts cannot have that value exercised
Read-only is enforced by the harness permission layer, not claimed in a prompt
The old git status contamination check is retired — the repo is never the working directory
Reps default to 1; the per-run abort timeout defaults to 300 seconds
Never name the section or file holding the fact in a query
Never put rubric text in a run prompt; the per-run prompt is the bare query
Never provide additional information beyond the query text, and never let the eval agent know it is a test
Keep the query verbatim within and across campaigns, {RUN_DIR} token included
Score from answer_text only; what the agent claims it did or found is not evidence
missed_bullets are copied character-for-character from the entry's expect list
ablation_flag derives mechanically as control == pass; classification is recorded if and only if result is fail
Every results.json entry id must be accounted for exactly once in scored.json
A missing skill-load signal is void, not fail; the doc was never in context
With reps > 1 the entry result is the worst non-void run outcome; an entry is void only if every run is void
A control pass is a flag, not a verdict; removal requires 3 consecutive control passes plus user confirmation

inventory-update: a control pass auto-marks a status-less fact status ablation streak 0 and increments the streak on a statused fact; a control fail clears an ablation fact's status and streak; a void control run neither increments nor resets
On removal: delete the fact text from SKILL.md, hand-edit the inventory item to status removed (streak continues, not reset), keep the entries as regression coverage
A query runs control-only when every fact covering it carries the same status; mixed-status queries run both arms
Ablation/removed queries run the control arm only; a control fail triggers a follow-up skill-arm suite without --manifest into the same campaign dir, merging by id
Doc fixes re-run only the failed entries as a mini-campaign in a confirm/round<N>/ subdir, with the queries file select-filtered to those entries
Mini-campaigns are never recorded, never passed to verify/record, and never touch ablation streaks
The counted results file is always named results.json; a superseded run is renamed results-superseded.json (then -2, ...) before re-running
Fact ids are minted by inventory-mint, never assigned by hand; they are section-anchored as F-<section-slug>-<nn>
The manifest is regenerated via the script whenever entries change and never hand-maintained; rebuild the inventory fresh from the doc every campaign as a diff baseline, never a cache
For <root>/.opencode/skills/<name> the source root is <root>/.opencode — the directory containing the skills/ dir
Queries and facts default under <source-root>/skills-workspace/<skill>/retrieval-tests/
Campaign artifacts (results, scored, snapshots) live in the persistent campaign dir under skills-workspace, never inside the temp eval workspaces
Each run gets the entry's fixture files copied fresh into its own run directory inside the eval workspace; no run ever writes into the repository
A {RUN_DIR} token requires a fixtures entry and fixtures require a token; the harness rejects the mismatch before any spend
Close-out order after a full campaign: scored.json, then inventory-update, then verify, then record; record runs only after verify exits 0
Findability fix: better headings, a TOC, a quick-reference row, one-level-deep references, move important reference content above line 100; never an always-read-X-first clause
Fix failures by editing the doc, never by adding behavioral rules, prohibitions, or discipline clauses
Apply doc fixes between campaigns after the full pass completes, only with user confirmation, never mid-campaign

Report layout: 'retrieval test: <skill> — <date>' header; queries:/artifacts:/manifest: lines; an id/result/control table; a 'summary: N pass / M fail / G gap / V void' line; then failures:, gaps:, ablation flags:, and regression failures: sections
Proposal cards: '## N. <entry-id>' with covers:/facts:/query:/expect:/why: lines, closed by coverage:/excluded:/cost:/fixtures: lines

excluded.reason: two arms in parallel with arm-tagged progress lines — harness-enforced mechanics, not an agent decision a prompt elicits
one suite process at a time enforced by a machine-wide lockfile — harness-enforced mechanics
verify's snapshot/wiring/scored-check consistency checks — harness-enforced consistency proof
record derives counts from the scored file, model/variant from results config, date from the campaign dir name — harness mechanics
the seven fact-keeper tests and drop/dedupe/cluster methodology — self-describing methodology, not reference-domain facts
derive queries from the failure mode, bait- or review-shaped — methodology guidance folded into authoring practice
result vocabulary pass/fail/gap/void — near-baseline vocabulary; the scored schema shape is exercised by the harness
'id — stable fact identifier; never reuse ids' — schema detail enforced by the harness
the harness measures bytes on disk so whether the driving session can load the skill is irrelevant — harness mechanics
a scenario still failing after a doc fix gets one more revision, then surface to the user — escalation policy, thinly testable and already implied by the fix rules
